hints.title: Give the two integrals short names
hints.body: Call the integral from 0 to 1 A and the integral from 1 to 2 B. Rewrite the first given equation using these two letters.
hints.recap: An unknown integral can be treated like any other unknown number.
hints.pitfall: An integral can be negative when the graph is below the axis.

recall.reminder: Signed integrals over adjacent intervals can be added and subtracted.

hints.title: Follow the x + 1 inside f
hints.body: In the second given integral, x goes from 0 to 1. Work out where x+1 starts and ends. This tells you which part of the original graph of f is being used.
hints.recap: A horizontal shift keeps the width and signed area of the matching region.
hints.pitfall: Use the limits for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> when matching it to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Identify the known integral, find the other one and add them for the full interval.

recall.reminder: A horizontal shift keeps the width and signed area of the matching region.

solution:
Write A=∫01f(x)dx and B=∫12f(x)dx. The shift in the second datum shows B=6.

Then 2A+5(6)=14, so A=−8. Combining adjacent intervals gives ∫02f(x)dx=A+B=−8+6=−2.

Answer C.
